# task-37e07c8b — dominoes slide toward the 2-band

## Rule
The solid color-2 line is a wall/boundary. Keep it unchanged. Each other colored 2-cell domino slides as far as possible in the direction toward that line (perpendicular to the band), stopping before the line or another domino. Empty cells remain 0. Thus a horizontal 2-band across row 0 sends dominoes upward; a vertical band down column 0 sends them left; a horizontal band at the bottom sends them down. Domino orientation stays unchanged. Separate dominoes of the same color are distinct movable shapes; they may touch/merge after landing. Do not rotate shapes.

## Demo evidence
- Demo 1: 10x6, color-2 band across bottom row. All colored dominoes slide down. For instance vertical 3 at col 0 landed rows 6–7; horizontal 8 landed row 6; horizontal 5 landed row 8. Output preserves blank rows, and the 2-band remains.
- Demo 2: 5x11, color-2 band down leftmost column. Dominoes slide left. Horizontal 3 landed at row 0, cols 1–2; vertical 5 at col 1; horizontal 6 at row 2, cols 2–3; vertical 8 at col 3; horizontal 7 at bottom, cols 1–2. Band stays fixed.
- Solved test: 10x10 band along top row. All dominoes slide upward, while maintaining relative placements where blocked. Notably, input had two distinct 6-dominoes (vertical at col 7 and horizontal near right edge); they packed adjacent under the band into a joined 3-cell run. Omitting the less obvious vertical 6 led to a wrong answer.

## Reliable procedure
1. Identify the uninterrupted 2-colored boundary line and its orientation/location.
2. Enumerate *every* other monochromatic 2-cell domino, including repeated colors and distant same-colored pieces. Record coordinates and orientation.
3. Move each domino parallel to the direction toward the band until the next step would hit the band, grid edge, or another occupied cell. Resolve packed configurations as sliding/settling, allowing separate pieces to come into contact but not overlap.
4. Preserve all occupied cells/colors and original dimensions; all other cells are zero, except the fixed 2-band.
5. Validate each domino appears exactly once and no output overlaps or changes shape/orientation. Particularly re-check repeated-color pieces that may join after sliding.

## Pitfall / corrected lesson
Do not drop a same-color domino from inventory because another domino of that color exists. The initially mistaken test prediction omitted the vertical 6 at (rows 1–2, col 7); once included, its two cells settled adjacent to the horizontal 6 and produced the correct output. Also, avoid interpreting the action as deleting pieces or moving them along the band; movement is perpendicular toward the 2-line.",
